title: J2 — Found at home
description: A health worker registers him offline and records the cards as "reported, not yet verified".

steps.title: A health worker finds the baby — and reads his cards
steps.headline: On a routine village visit, Vilay finds a newborn the Lao system doesn’t know exists. She can read the vaccines on his cards, but she can’t prove they are genuine.
steps.narrative:
On a routine visit to Village 04, Vilay finds a newborn the Lao
system does not know exists. Her phone has had no signal for weeks. Khamla
shows the two cards. The CHW app reads them with **read-unverified**
(STT-VER-011; STT-B45-002, STT-ZIP-002, STT-CBR-003), which needs no trust
list. It shows the doses, but checks no signature and saves nothing yet.

experiences.doing: Tells Vilay about the birth in Thailand and shows the cards.
experiences.feeling: “I hope we’re not in trouble for giving birth abroad.”

experiences.doing: Scans both QR cards and reads the doses, without checking their signatures.
experiences.feeling: “I can read it, but I can’t prove it’s real out here.”

steps.painPoint: Without a check, a forged or mistyped card could quietly become an official record.
steps.enabler: The phone reads the card offline, and keeps “what the family told us” clearly separate from “what we have verified”.
steps.policy: Keep a clear line between what families report and what has been verified, and don’t grant trust too early.

record.description: Doses read from the 2 cards; nothing saved yet

handoff.summary: The doses, read but not checked, go into the registration

whatIf.scenario: What if the CHW phone could verify signatures offline too?
whatIf.outcome: Technically possible with a cached trust list — but who keeps it current on thousands of village phones?

steps.technicalSummary: The phone can read the QR but deliberately doesn’t trust it: it decodes the card offline and checks no signature. Nothing is written yet.

uses.role: QR decoded (CBOR) but signature not checked
PreQual codes read, but not yet mapped to the Lao schedule

steps.title: Registered at home, and referred
steps.headline: With no signal, Vilay adds Somsack to his household, saves his doses as “reported”, and refers the family to the clinic.
steps.narrative:
On the CHW app's newborn form (structured data capture,
`TrustDemoHouseholdRegistration`) she adds Somsack to the Sengmany household
(`TrustDemoHousehold`), with a temporary id. Bounmy confirms the details as
head of household. The app saves the doses read from the cards as reported by
the family, not verified (`TrustDemoJ2HepBReported`, `TrustDemoJ2BcgReported`:
`primarySource` false). Vilay refers Somsack to the district health center
(`TrustDemoJ2Referral`). Everything stays queued on the phone, for 28 days if
need be, and syncs when it next reaches a signal.

experiences.doing: Adds Somsack to the Sengmany household, saves the two doses as unverified and books a clinic referral.
experiences.feeling: “No signal for weeks — but I need to register him today.”

experiences.doing: Is added to his household: the Lao health system now knows he exists.
experiences.feeling: “Three weeks old, and now he counts.”

experiences.doing: Confirms household details as head of household.
experiences.feeling: “Good, he’s on our family record now.”

experiences.doing: Receives a referral to the District Health Center.
experiences.feeling: “Another trip — but at least they know about his vaccines now.”

steps.painPoint: Babies born abroad are invisible to the home health system until civil registration catches up — sometimes months later.
steps.enabler: An offline form links the baby to his household immediately; it syncs once the phone finds a signal.
steps.policy: Newborns can be registered at home, offline, before civil registration or a national ID exists.

record.description: Baby registered; 2 doses saved as “reported by family”

handoff.summary: Referral to the District Health Center
handoff.carrier: Offline form (FHIR Questionnaire), then sync via Info Gateway

whatIf.scenario: Vilay’s phone stays offline for 28 days.
whatIf.outcome: Everything stays queued safely on the device and syncs when she next reaches the health center.

steps.technicalSummary: The registration form is a FHIR Questionnaire. Its answers become standard FHIR resources on the phone; the doses read from the cards are saved with primarySource=false, apart from verified data, and everything syncs whenever there is signal.

uses.role: Stores data on the phone; works 28+ days offline
Renders the household registration form and extracts FHIR from the answers
Patient and Group (household); Immunization.primarySource = false; ServiceRequest for referral
On sync, checks the CHW’s token and only lets her write to households in her own catchment
